spans.text: The torrential rain leaves you thoroughly drenched, but you're unfazed by it.
Droplets of rainwater splash loudly as they hit the tree leaves. As you make your way through the woods, you can hear distant peals of thunder every now and then.
All this is for the sake of the girl who's waiting under the pavilion.
...I didn't expect there to be such a huge storm tonight, but I didn't want anyone else to overhear what I wanted to say.
I'm sorry for not considering the fact that you are human.
It's alright... I've seen much crazier weather than this at my previous workplace.
You don't have to worry about it... So, what do you want to tell me that need to be said all the way out here?
Before that, I want to ask you a question. How do you feel about suddenly becoming our manager?
...I guess you saw through me. It's true, I was forced into it.
I knew it.
But being a manager isn't easy. You can't just train up an amateur for a couple of days and then push them into the position.
...Er, but if I'm not wrong, the rest of Franchouchou isn't exactly...
Yes, and it's precisely because we have a few unpolished members that we can't afford to have a half-baked manager.
So should I go take a class or something?
I think it's a little late for that, don't you think...?
...There's no need for that. Relax, I don't expect anyone to make any breakthroughs or anything. That sort of thing can't be done easily in the short term anyway.
All I need you to do is nothing.
Hm? What does that mean?
I'll prepare the training plans and perform all the manager's work ahead of time.
Just so we don't cause the others any alarm, you'll do the talking, but I'll have everything prepared for you.
In return, don't do anything else.
I'll take care of everything, and once our show next week is a success, you can return to where you came from.
...That does sound pretty good.
It's decided, then.
But I disagree.
Huh? Why is that?
Do you actually think anyone can be a manager?
Don't you dare look down on the hard work it takes to become a manager!
I'm not!
In fact, that's all the more reason why I can't just dump all the work onto you.
If you've got extra time, you should spend it on training and practicing with the others.
You shouldn't be wasting your energy on doing things that I should have done in the first place.
...It's good that you feel that way. However—
I'll be frank. I'd rather spend more time on doing extra things than let the others be led astray by unprofessional opinions.
I fully understand your concerns.
If I were at Griffin and some civilian suddenly came up to me and said they wanted to be a commander, I'd say no too.
But... I hope you can try to have some faith in me.
I can't guarantee that I'll become a perfect manager, but I promise that I won't hold you back and that I'll do everything I can to help Franchouchou.
I know all this just sounds like pretty words, and I don't intend to convince you with words alone.
I'll prove myself through my actions.
Please give me a chance. Let me show that I can keep up with Franchouchou's pace over the next three days.
If I can't do it in three days, then you can kick me out!
If three days is too long, then two will do!
...I see. Well, it makes no difference whether it's two days or three.
Alright, I accept your proposal.
However, you'd better remember what you said today.
Thank you!
No, I should be thanking you.
At first, I thought you wouldn't be motivated to do anything, seeing that you were suddenly roped into all this.
But as it turns out... it seems I've underestimated you.
Whap—
Ai opens the transparent umbrella that she's holding. There is an almost imperceptible smile on her face.
Let's head back. You ought to change your clothes too. You can't afford to spend these three days you've earned yourself being sick.
You look at her and open your mouth to speak before silently getting under her umbrella with her.
As the rain gradually eases off, the two of you head back to the mansion.
